name: Grammarly
tagline: Writing help, rewriting and tone control in every draft
description: Grammarly checks grammar, clarity and tone across browser, desktop and mobile, with AI rewriting and shared style guides that keep a team writing consistently.
priceNote: Pro is $12 per member/month billed annually ($144 per year) or $30 month-to-month; Business sits around $12 per user/month on annual billing and Enterprise is quoted. Pricing as of October 2026; plans change — check the official site.
bestFor: Teams that write a lot of customer-facing copy and want one shared style
pros: It catches grammar and clarity issues in Gmail, Word and Slack without changing the workflow
AI rewriting and tone control turn a clumsy first draft into a sendable one in a click
Style guides and snippets keep every writer using the same terms and phrasing
A free tier handles the basics, so a single user can start at no cost
cons: The free tier is limited enough that a heavy writer hits the wall within days
Per-member billing means a company-wide rollout is a line item that grows with headcount
It flags many false positives on technical and legal wording, which trains people to ignore it
Support moved to a different company after the rebrand, and the quality of answers varies

features.name: Grammar and clarity checks
features.detail: Context-aware suggestions across email, documents and chat

features.name: AI rewriting
features.detail: Rewrite for tone, length and formality without leaving the draft

features.name: Style guides
features.detail: Team rules for terms, structure and tone applied to every suggestion

features.name: Generative drafting
features.detail: Draft, summarise and rewrite paragraphs from a short instruction

features.name: Works where you write
features.detail: Browser extension, desktop app, mobile keyboard and Word add-in

features.name: Brand and tone controls
features.detail: Custom vocabulary and tone preferences per team or account

useCases: Catch awkward customer emails before they leave the founder's inbox
Keep a small agency client-facing copy consistent across five freelancers
Polish sales follow-ups written fast on a phone during a trade show
Turn a long internal document into a summary a client will actually read
bestForWho: Written-heavy roles such as support, sales and marketing that need fast, consistent editing without a copywriter.
verdict: Grammarly is one of those tools that looks optional until you notice how many awkward emails were caught on the way out, and for a team that writes to customers all day it pays for itself quickly. The AI rewriting and tone controls are the part I use most, since fixing tone in one click beats hunting for the right word. Style guides are what make it a team tool rather than a personal one, because they stop five freelancers describing the same feature five different ways. The limitation is that it flags plenty of false positives on technical, legal and non-native phrasing, which gradually teaches writers to dismiss the suggestions without reading them. Billed per member, it is cheap for a small team and obvious in the budget for a fifty-person company.
